description: Hot and Sour Soup is a beloved classic in Chinese cuisine, famous for its tantalizing balance of spicy chili and tangy vinegar flavors. This comforting soup features a rich broth brimming with tender tofu, earthy mushrooms, and delicate shreds of meat, all thickened to perfection. It is a truly invigorating dish that awakens the palate with every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried wood ear and shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 20-30 minutes. Drain, trim any tough stems, and slice them thinly. Dice the firm tofu into 1/2-inch cubes, thinly shred the pork loin, and prepare the shredded bamboo shoots. In separate small bowls, prepare the cornstarch slurry by dissolving cornstarch in water, and beat the egg.

instructions.title: Simmer Broth and Main Ingredients
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring the chicken broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Add the sliced wood ear mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, shredded pork, and bamboo shoots to the simmering broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes, ensuring the pork is fully cooked through and the mushrooms are tender.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Stir in the rice vinegar, light soy sauce, white pepper, and chili oil. Taste the soup and adjust the seasonings to your preference. You may add more rice vinegar for extra tanginess or more chili oil for a spicier kick, depending on your desired balance of hot and sour flavors.

instructions.title: Thicken the Soup
instructions.text: Slowly pour the prepared cornstarch slurry into the simmering soup while continuously stirring the soup. Continue to stir gently until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. This process should take just a few minutes.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Egg Ribbons
instructions.text: Gently add the diced firm tofu to the thickened soup, being careful not to break the cubes. Next, slowly drizzle the beaten egg into the hot soup in a thin, steady stream while stirring the soup gently in one direction. This will create delicate, fine egg ribbons throughout the soup.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the sesame oil, which adds a wonderful aromatic finish. Ladle the hot Hot and Sour Soup into individual serving bowls and garnish generously with freshly chopped green onions before serving immediately.

tips: For an authentic taste, use good quality rice vinegar and freshly ground white pepper. Adjust the spiciness and sourness gradually to find your perfect balance.
If you dont eat pork, shredded chicken breast or extra mushrooms can be used. For a vegetarian version, use vegetable broth and omit the pork and egg.
Hot and Sour Soup is best served immediately. If reheating, add a splash of broth or water as it might thicken further and adjust seasonings if needed.
article:
When it comes to the vast and varied world of Chinese cuisine, few dishes capture the imagination and tantalize the taste buds quite like Hot and Sour Soup. It's a culinary paradox in a bowl – simultaneously fiery and tangy, rich and light, comforting and invigorating. This beloved classic, found on menus from bustling street stalls to elegant fine dining establishments, offers a symphony of flavors and textures that leaves an unforgettable impression. If you're looking for an authentic Hot and Sour Soup Recipe that brings the restaurant experience right into your kitchen, you've come to the right place.

Hot and Sour Soup isn't just a starter; it's an experience. Its unique balance of piquant heat and sharp sourness, coupled with a delightful array of ingredients, makes it a perennial favorite. Dive into the heart of this iconic dish as we explore its origins, essential components, and guide you through crafting your very own perfect bowl.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

Hot and Sour Soup, or Suan La Tang (酸辣汤) in Mandarin, is a quintessential Chinese soup renowned for its intriguing flavor profile. Originating from the Sichuan and Hunan provinces of China, regions famous for their bold and spicy dishes, it has since become a staple across the globe. The "hot" typically comes from white pepper and, optionally, a touch of chili oil or dried chilies, providing a deep, warming heat rather than an aggressive burn. The "sour" is primarily derived from Chinese black vinegar or rice vinegar, offering a pungent, tangy kick that brightens the entire soup.

Beyond its distinctive taste, the soup is celebrated for its medley of textures. Silken strands of egg, tender shreds of pork or chicken, crunchy wood ear mushrooms, crisp bamboo shoots, and soft tofu cubes create a dynamic mouthfeel that keeps every spoonful interesting. The broth itself is usually thickened slightly with cornstarch, giving it a comforting, velvety consistency that coats the palate beautifully. It’s a dish that embodies the Chinese culinary philosophy of balancing contrasting elements to create a harmonious whole.

## Ingredients for Hot and Sour Soup

Crafting the perfect Hot and Sour Soup begins with selecting the right ingredients. While variations exist, the core components remain consistent, each playing a crucial role in achieving that signature flavor and texture.

For a classic Hot and Sour Soup Recipe, you'll typically need:

*   **Broth:** 6-8 cups of good quality chicken broth or vegetable broth. A rich broth forms the foundation of your soup.
*   **Protein:** 4-6 oz pork loin or tenderloin, thinly shredded; or chicken breast, similarly shredded. For a vegetarian version, extra firm tofu works wonderfully.
*   **Mushrooms:** 1 oz dried wood ear mushrooms and/or dried shiitake mushrooms. Rehydrate these until soft, then slice thinly. They provide essential texture and umami.
*   **Bamboo Shoots:** 1/2 cup canned bamboo shoots, julienned.
*   **Tofu:** 4 oz firm or silken tofu, cut into small cubes.
*   **Flavorings:**
    *   3-4 tbsp light soy sauce (for saltiness and color)
    *   1 tbsp dark soy sauce (for deeper color and a touch of sweetness)
    *   1/4 cup Chinese black vinegar or rice vinegar (the primary sour agent)
    *   2-3 tbsp white pepper (crucial for the "hot" element)
    *   1-2 tbsp sesame oil (for aroma and nutty finish)
    *   1-2 tsp chili oil (optional, for extra heat)
*   **Thickener:** 3-4 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/2 cup cold water (cornstarch slurry).
*   **Egg:** 2 large eggs, lightly beaten.
*   **Garnish:** 2-3 green onions, thinly sliced; fresh cilantro (optional).

## Step-by-Step: How to Make Hot and Sour Soup

Embarking on your own Hot and Sour Soup Recipe journey is simpler than you might think. With a little preparation and attention to detail, you can recreate this restaurant favorite at home.

1.  **Preparation is Key:** Start by rehydrating your dried mushrooms according to package instructions (usually soaking in hot water for 20-30 minutes). Once soft, squeeze out excess water and slice them thinly. Prepare your other ingredients: shred the pork/chicken, julienne the bamboo shoots, cube the tofu, slice the green onions. In a small bowl, whisk the eggs. In another, mix the cornstarch with cold water to create a smooth slurry.
2.  **Cook the Protein (Optional):** If using pork or chicken, you can quickly blanch it in boiling water for a minute or two, then drain. This helps keep the broth clear. Alternatively, you can add it directly to the simmering broth.
3.  **Simmer the Broth:** Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into a large pot and bring it to a boil. Add the rehydrated mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu. Reduce heat and let it simmer for 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
4.  **Season the Soup:** Stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and a generous amount of white pepper. This is where the "hot" truly begins. Add the Chinese black vinegar. Taste and adjust seasonings – you might want more soy sauce, pepper, or vinegar to suit your preference. Remember, the flavors will deepen.
5.  **Thicken the Broth:** Give your cornstarch slurry a quick whisk again (it tends to settle). Slowly pour the slurry into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly, until the soup reaches your desired consistency. It should be slightly thickened, not overly gloopy.
6.  **Add Egg Ribbons:** Once the soup is thickened, increase the heat slightly. While gently stirring the soup in a circular motion, slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream. The hot broth will cook the egg into delicate ribbons. Stop stirring once the egg is fully cooked, about 30 seconds.
7.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the soup from the heat. Stir in the sesame oil and chili oil (if using). Ladle the hot soup into bowls and garnish generously with fresh green onions and, if desired, a sprinkle of cilantro. This Hot and Sour Soup Recipe is best enjoyed immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Hot and Sour Soup

Mastering this Hot and Sour Soup Recipe involves paying attention to a few key details that elevate it from good to truly exceptional.

*   **Don't Skimp on White Pepper:** White pepper is the primary source of the "hot" in this soup, providing a unique pungency different from chili heat. Be generous; it's a defining characteristic.
*   **Balance the Sour:** Add the vinegar in stages. Some prefer a stronger sour kick, while others like it more subtle. A final splash of vinegar right before serving can brighten the flavor even further.
*   **Quality Broth:** A homemade chicken broth will always yield the best results, but a good quality store-bought broth (low sodium is often best) is a great alternative.
*   **Consistency is Key:** Adjust the cornstarch slurry carefully. You want a velvety texture, not a thick stew. You can always add more slurry if needed, but it's hard to thin it out once it's too thick.
*   **Experiment with Heat:** While white pepper is essential, a touch of chili oil or a few dried chili flakes can add another layer of warmth for those who like it extra spicy.
*   **Freshness Matters for Garnish:** Freshly sliced green onions and cilantro not only add color but also a burst of fresh flavor and aroma that complements the rich soup.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Traditionally, it serves as a robust appetizer, kicking off a larger Chinese meal. Its bold flavors awaken the palate, preparing it for subsequent dishes.

As a light meal on its own, especially during colder months, it's incredibly comforting. You can pair it with a simple bowl of steamed white rice, which helps to mellow the intensity of the soup. Other excellent pairings include:

*   **Spring Rolls or Egg Rolls:** The crispiness of fried appetizers contrasts beautifully with the soup's silky texture.
*   **Dumplings or Potstickers:** A classic combination, offering different textures and flavors that complement each other.
*   **Fried Rice or Lo Mein:** For a more substantial meal, a side of fried rice or noodles makes for a satisfying spread.
*   **Stir-fries:** Its zesty profile cuts through the richness of many stir-fried dishes.

Garnish your soup with extra chili oil, a dash of toasted sesame seeds, or even a few drops of hot sauce for an added personal touch.

## Variations and Substitutions

The beauty of this Hot and Sour Soup Recipe lies in its adaptability. Don't be afraid to experiment and make it your own!

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Easily make this soup meat-free by using vegetable broth and omitting the pork/chicken. Increase the amount of tofu, and consider adding more varieties of mushrooms (like oyster or button) for extra umami. For a vegan version, simply omit the egg, and it will still be delicious.
*   **Different Proteins:** Instead of pork or chicken, try shredded duck, shrimp, or even thinly sliced beef.
*   **Mushroom Medley:** Explore other dried or fresh mushrooms like enoki, king oyster, or crimini for varied textures and depths of flavor.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the white pepper to your liking. For an extra kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes or increase the amount of chili oil.
*   **Vinegar Options:** While Chinese black vinegar is traditional, rice vinegar is a common substitute. Some recipes even use a touch of Worcestershire sauce for a different kind of tang and depth.
*   **Keto/Low-Carb:** To make this Hot and Sour Soup Recipe keto-friendly, omit the cornstarch or use a keto-approved thickener like xanthan gum (use sparingly, as it's much more potent).

Armed with this comprehensive Hot and Sour Soup Recipe, you're now ready to embark on a flavorful journey. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a kitchen novice, the reward of a steaming bowl of homemade Hot and Sour Soup is immense. It's a dish that truly embodies the heart and soul of Chinese cooking – bold, balanced, and utterly delicious. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with this timeless classic.
